turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm debugging a weird issue with the SessionTeardown logic today. It seems like the shutdown sequence is messy.
That sounds tricky. What specifically looks wrong in the sequence?

Well, I traced it this morning. I realized that SessionTeardown's drain method closes admission, drains in-flight tasks with an external timeout, persists pending items, shuts down the pool without waiting, and closes caches in LIFO order.
Got it, so the LIFO order for caches and the non-waiting pool shutdown are key parts of the current implementation. Did you change anything else?
No, just confirming the current behavior. Oh, unrelated, did my package for the new mechanical keyboard arrive yet?
I don't have real-time shipping access, but you can check your carrier tracking link I sent earlier.
Right, I'll check it. Thanks for listening to the code rant.
No problem. Let me know if you need help refactoring that drain method later.
Lloyd, I was reading the ReaSearch paper today and noticed something interesting about the authors.
It turns out Snowflake is an affiliation for several authors of the ReaSearch paper.
That makes sense given their work in data infrastructure. Did you find the methodology interesting otherwise?
Yeah, quite solid. Anyway, I'm heading out for lunch now. Pizza?
Enjoy your lunch! Let me know if you want to discuss the paper's results later.
Will do. Just wanted to drop that tidbit in my notes.
